content:
A few months ago, a stranger messaged me on LinkedIn.

I expected the usual “great post” message.

Instead, they said they’d been reading my content for a while and wanted to work with me.

That message stayed with me !!

Because at that point, I was still sitting in college classrooms, worrying about attendance, assignments and exams.

My résumé didn’t have much to say.

But my work did :))

I had been writing on LinkedIn, creating on Instagram, experimenting, building an audience and putting my thoughts out there consistently.

Someone had seen that before they ever saw my degree.

And I think that says something about our generation.

There are students creating content after class, building audiences from their bedrooms, freelancing between lectures, launching businesses, sharing their work online and building portfolios before they even graduate.

They’re not waiting for someone to give them a title.

They’re creating their own proof.

College is still part of the journey.

It just isn’t the whole journey anymore.

A résumé tells people what you’ve done.

Your work shows them what you can do.

I’m still a student.

But I’m also building something people can see.

And maybe that’s what’s different now.

We don’t have to wait for the world to call us professionals before we start doing professional work.

We can build it.
Share it.
Let people find it.

And let the work introduce us before the résumé ever does :)
comment: A portfolio can open doors, but the next challenge is proving consistency at scale—turning visible work into repeatable skills, judgment, and outcomes that teams can rely on.
